# Testament of Judah — 4
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Judah was the strongest of Jacob's sons — the fighter, the leader, the one destined for kingship. His testament is also the most honest. He confesses two weaknesses that undid him: wine and women. And he knows exactly how they worked.

**1** These are the dying words of Judah to his sons.

**2** He said: I am Judah. My mother named me Thanksgiving — she said, I give thanks to the LORD. I was quick and obedient as a boy. I honored my father in everything, and he blessed me: You will be a king. God prospered everything I touched.

**3** I fought with lions and bears. I caught a deer and brought it to my father. I slew a leopard and rescued a lamb. I beat bears over cliffs with my bare hands. In battle I fought giants. I slew Achor the king — a man of enormous stature — with his own shield. I pursued and conquered kings.

**4** But I had three weaknesses: wine, women, and money. And each one nearly destroyed me.

**5** First: Bathshua. My friend Hirah introduced me. Her father was a king who paraded his daughter before me with gold and pearls and had her pour my wine. The wine clouded my eyes and pleasure blinded my heart. I lay with her against my father's wishes and the commandment of the LORD. The LORD gave me no joy from those sons — Er and Onan, he took them in their wickedness. Only Shelah survived.

**6** Second: Tamar. This is harder to tell.

**7** After eighteen years, while Bathshua was still alive, I got drunk with Hirah the Adullamite. I came into town and saw a woman sitting at the city gate, adorned and veiled. I didn't know it was Tamar, my own daughter-in-law, the widow of my son — I was too drunk to recognize her. **8** I turned aside to her. She asked what I'd give. I gave her my staff, my belt, and the signet of my kingdom. I slept with her and she conceived.

**9** When I found out she was pregnant, I was furious. I almost had her killed. But she sent my pledges back to me — and I knew. I knew what I'd done. She was more righteous than I was. She had done what she did because I had withheld my son Shelah from her.

**10** From that day, I drank no wine until I was old. Not a drop. Because I knew: it was the wine that did it. Wine turns the mind away from truth. Wine unlocks the spirit of lust. They work together — wine and desire — and together they destroy a man.

**11** A drunk man fears no one. He has no shame. He doesn't remember his father's commands or the commands of God. He acts in daylight what he would be ashamed to do in darkness.

**12** So hear me: do not love money and do not stare at women's beauty. Those are the two paths that brought me — Judah, the king — into shame. And they will bring my descendants into captivity. Even the wise among my sons will be led astray by these two things. The kingdom God gave me because I obeyed my father — it will be diminished because my descendants won't.

**13** I read it in the books of Enoch. I know what is coming.

**14** These sins — lust and greed — they steal your compassion. They make you arrogant. They rob your soul of goodness. They fill your nights with grinding anxiety and your days with distraction. They cut you off from prayer, from the prophets, from the blessing of God. They make you serve two masters at once, and you end up serving neither — least of all God.

**15** So: keep the LORD's commands. Honor Levi. Do it for your own safety.

**16** Because from Judah and Levi, salvation will come to all Israel. The LORD will raise up from Levi a High Priest, and from Judah a King — God and man together — and he will save every nation and the whole house of Israel.

---
*End of Testament of Judah*
